label: GPT-6.1 Terra
output:
To: board:vendor-reviews
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Harbor Point Steno Service, Towson — Aria 3 recalibration

Dana, I promised I would report back once I had put my writer through a real trial. It has now been through eight days of a civil trial, and I would trust Harbor Point with an Aria 3 again, with one reservation about being able to reach the shop by phone.

I dropped off my Stenvale Aria 3 on Monday, October 19, for a full recalibration and a look at the number bar. Harbor Point quoted $285 and an estimated 10 business days. I picked it up Tuesday, October 27, six business days later. The final bill was $310, which I paid myself by card, as I do for all my equipment. The court did not reimburse me.

The work included a full keyboard recalibration, replacement of the number bar depression sensor, internal cleaning, and a firmware update. Gloria also found that the internal battery was holding about 60% of its rated capacity. She emailed to ask before replacing it, and I approved the additional $25. That matters to me. I think $310 was fair for the work done.

The machine came back with a printed, one-page service sheet listing every adjustment. I have never had that from anyone before, and I appreciated having a record I could take home. The work carries a 90-day warranty.

The first full day back was expert testimony from an engineer who talks in numbers. The number bar did not double a single stroke. It has held up through the eight days of trial, which is a better test than anything I could have done at my kitchen table. Dana, given the trouble you described with your number bar, I would be comfortable taking your Aria there based on my experience.

Harbor Point did provide a loaner, an Aria 2. It got me through, but the tilt arm slipped mid-afternoon during a deposition, and I had to prop it up with a legal pad for the rest of the day. I told Gloria, and she said they would repair it before it goes out again. If you need the loaner, I would check the arm when you pick it up.

The real weakness is the phone situation. I called Wednesday, October 21, to ask about progress. It rang out, and there was no voicemail box set up. Gloria emailed the following day, but I could not leave a message when I called. Their phone is staffed only Tuesday through Thursday, 9 to 4, which is a particular problem if you are working a Monday docket and need an answer that day.

It is a two-person shop off York Road, with free parking in back. Gloria did good work, the price and turnaround were reasonable, and she asked before adding to the bill. I would use them again, but I would plan around those phone hours rather than count on reaching someone whenever I need to.

Maureen
